description: Dock and sidebar layout commands, appearance, window commands, the welcome and agent views, and the layout state path.

commands.title: Move tab back into the main window
Move all tabs back into the main window
Hide the welcome page's import link

enumDescriptions: Ask once when a folder you haven't decided about opens (VS Code's default)
Don't ask when a folder opens; ask before its first task, debug session or test run
security.workspace.trust.startupPrompt.description: When to ask whether you trust the authors of a folder's files.
security.workspace.trust.startupPrompt.title: Ask about trust when a folder opens

security.warnRiskyFolders.description: Before your Downloads folder (or a folder in it), your home folder, the Desktop, the temp folder or the root of a drive opens as the workspace, explain the risk and offer restricted mode. Files a browser saves there can hold instructions written to trick AI agents. Agents ask before working in those folders either way.
security.warnRiskyFolders.title: Warn before opening a risky folder

security.riskyFolders.description: More folders that count like Downloads (absolute paths; the folders inside them too): where another browser or a mail program saves files.
security.riskyFolders.title: Other risky folders

enumDescriptions: Check a minute after start and once a day; offer a newer version (nothing downloads until you install it)
Only when you choose Help → Check for updates…
Never
update.mode.description: Updates (release builds made with an update server; development builds never check).
update.mode.title: Updates

enumDescriptions: Released versions
Previews of the next version, earlier and less tested (when this build has a beta channel; otherwise stable)
update.channel.title: Update channel

workbench.theme.description: Deprecated: replaced by workbench.colorTheme ("Dark+" / "Light+"). Still read when workbench.colorTheme is empty.

workbench.scrollbarSize.description: Width of scrollbars outside the editor and terminal (lists, panels, pages), in pixels. The editor's and the terminal's have their own settings.

workbench.panels.description: Flush: one shell color with 1px dividers. Floating: panels as cards with gaps.

enumDescriptions: The panels' color, like the editors and the bottom panel
The color theme's side bar color, set apart from the panels
workbench.sideBarColor.title: Side bar color
workbench.sideBarColor.description: The side bar's color, with flush or floating panels: matching the panels, or the color theme's own side bar color.

enumDescriptions: Rounded tabs inside the tab strip
Square tabs side by side, with the accent along the active tab's top
The active tab joins the editor under it, on a lighter tab strip
workbench.tabStyle.title: Tab style
workbench.tabStyle.description: The look of the tabs on editors, terminals and the other views in the dock.

workbench.colorTheme.description: The color theme: Claude Dark (the default), Dark+ or Light+ (built in), a bundled Shiki theme, or one from an installed extension (VS Code themes work).

window.autoDetectColorScheme.title: Follow the system's light or dark mode
window.autoDetectColorScheme.description: Use `workbench.preferredDarkColorTheme` while the system is in dark mode and `workbench.preferredLightColorTheme` in light mode, instead of `workbench.colorTheme`.

workbench.preferredDarkColorTheme.title: Preferred dark color theme
workbench.preferredDarkColorTheme.description: The theme for the system's dark mode, when `window.autoDetectColorScheme` is on.

workbench.preferredLightColorTheme.title: Preferred light color theme
workbench.preferredLightColorTheme.description: The theme for the system's light mode, when `window.autoDetectColorScheme` is on.

workbench.iconTheme.description: File icon theme: Material Icon Theme (built in), Minimal (the IDE's own small set), or one from an installed extension (VS Code icon themes work).

workbench.productIconTheme.description: Product icon theme (VS Code's): Default (the IDE's own icons) or one from an installed extension, whose font redraws the workbench's icons.

workbench.colorCustomizations.description: Colors over the theme: design tokens ({ "--accent": "#5FB3A1" }) or VS Code color ids (titleBar.activeBackground, activityBar.background, statusBar.background and their foregrounds, as Peacock writes them; editor.background, focusBorder…). A "[Theme name]" block applies only under that theme. The folder's value is merged over the user's.

workbench.editor.enablePreview.description: Single-clicking a file opens it in a preview tab (italic title) that the next preview replaces. Editing or double-clicking keeps it.

workbench.editor.decorations.colors.title: Tab decorations: colors
workbench.editor.decorations.colors.description: Color tab titles by the file's git status and problems (errors, warnings), as in the explorer.

workbench.editor.decorations.badges.title: Tab decorations: badges
workbench.editor.decorations.badges.description: Show the file's git status letter and problem count after the tab title.

workbench.editor.tabActionLocation.title: Tab close button location
workbench.editor.tabActionLocation.description: Which side of the tab title the close button is on.

workbench.editor.tabActionCloseVisibilit.title: Tab close button
workbench.editor.tabActionCloseVisibilit.description: Show a close button on tabs (on the active tab and on hover). Off: close with the middle mouse button, Ctrl+W or the tab's menu.

workbench.editor.pinnedTabsOnSeparateRow.title: Pinned tabs on a separate row
workbench.editor.pinnedTabsOnSeparateRow.description: Show pinned tabs on their own row above the other tabs.

enumDescriptions: Above the editor, side by side
A list on the group's left, one tab per row
A list on the group's right, one tab per row
workbench.editor.tabPlacement.title: Tab placement

workbench.editor.limit.enabled.title: Limit open tabs
workbench.editor.limit.enabled.description: Close the least recently used tabs when more than `workbench.editor.limit.value` are open. Pinned tabs, and tabs with unsaved changes, stay.

workbench.editor.limit.value.title: Limit: tabs
workbench.editor.limit.value.description: The most tabs kept open when the limit is on.

workbench.editor.limit.perEditorGroup.title: Limit: per group
workbench.editor.limit.perEditorGroup.description: Count each group's tabs on their own instead of all groups' together.

workbench.editor.limit.excludeDirty.title: Limit: don't count unsaved tabs
workbench.editor.limit.excludeDirty.description: Tabs with unsaved changes don't count toward the limit.

workbench.editor.focusRecentEditorAfterC.title: Focus the most recent tab after closing
workbench.editor.focusRecentEditorAfterC.description: After closing a tab, show the tab used most recently. Off: the tab to its right (or left, at the end).

workbench.navigationControl.enabled.title: Back and forward buttons
workbench.navigationControl.enabled.description: Show the Go back and Go forward buttons (Alt+Left / Alt+Right).

enumDescriptions: Beside the search box in the title bar
At the start of each group's tab strip
workbench.navigationControl.location.title: Back and forward buttons: location
workbench.navigationControl.location.description: Where the Go back and Go forward buttons are.

workbench.activityBar.hidden.description: Sidebar views hidden from the activity bar (right-click an icon to hide or show it). A hidden view that belongs under another (Timeline, Outline) stays there as a collapsed section.

workbench.activityBar.order.description: Order of the sidebar views on the activity bar, as view ids (drag an icon to change it). Views not listed come after, in their default order.

workbench.view.alwaysShowHeaderActions.description: Always show the buttons in view and panel headers (sidebar views and their sections, editor groups, the title bar's layout toggles). Off: they appear when you hover or focus the view.

window.zoomLevel.description: Zoom of the whole window: 0 is 100 %, each step up or down is 20 % (Ctrl+= / Ctrl+-).

workbench.sideBar.location.description: Which side of the window the activity bar and sidebar (explorer, search…) are on.

enumDescriptions: The chats list, the welcome page, and the agent's chat on the right.
The chats list and the agent's chat, filling the window.
The welcome page alone, as VS Code starts; the explorer shows once a folder is open.
workbench.defaultLayout.title: Default layout
workbench.defaultLayout.description: What a window starts with: when it opens without a folder, when a folder is closed, and the first time a folder is opened. A folder opened before keeps the layout it had.

workbench.openReadme.description: When a folder is opened for the first time, show its README (as a preview).

workbench.statusBar.visible.title: Status bar
workbench.statusBar.visible.description: Show the status bar at the bottom of the window.

workbench.statusBar.hidden.title: Hidden status bar items
workbench.statusBar.hidden.description: Status bar items hidden by their id (right-click the status bar to hide or show one).

workbench.editor.centeredLayout.title: Centered layout
workbench.editor.centeredLayout.description: Keep text editors at a readable width in the middle of wide editor groups.
